ACCOUNT_CUTOVER_ENFORCEMENT: default-off is correct: utils/account_cutover/access.py:30 defaults to 'off'. It enforces the legacy whole-account cutover upstream is running as a migration; a self-host has no legacy accounts to cut over, and turning it on would gate access on a state no user here has.
ACCOUNT_DELETION_DISPATCH_MODE: default-ok, and it is the default that makes account deletion work here: utils/cloud_tasks.py:89 reads it with default 'inline', i.e. run the handler in-process instead of enqueueing to GCP Cloud Tasks. Setting it to the queue mode on-prem would enqueue into a service that does not exist. The three variables that configure that queue (HANDLER_URL, TASKS_QUEUE, and the invoker SA) are unreachable from the inline path.
ACCOUNT_DELETION_HANDLER_URL: default-ok: only read on the Cloud Tasks dispatch path, which is off on-prem (see ACCOUNT_DELETION_DISPATCH_MODE).
ACCOUNT_DELETION_TASKS_QUEUE: default-ok: names a GCP Cloud Tasks queue, unreachable from the inline dispatch path we run.
ADMIN_KEY: leave it UNSET -- that is fail-closed, and the difference between unset and empty is real. Measured in the live container: with ADMIN_KEY unset, _require_admin_key('whatever') and ('') both raise 403; only None is accepted, and every admin route declares `secret_key: str = Header(...)`, so None cannot arrive over HTTP. Declaring ADMIN_KEY= (EMPTY) would open them: the bare `secret_key != os.getenv('ADMIN_KEY')` form used by memory_admin, apps, notifications and updates then accepts an empty `secret_key:` header -- measured. announcements.py and updates.py:1324 already carry the hardened form (`if not admin_key or ...`). Our env files declare it nowhere, which is the right answer; the divergence between the two comparison forms is upstream's and is tracked in L48.
BETA_PROMOTION_TOKEN: default-ok: gates the desktop Beta promotion endpoint; unset, the endpoint refuses. We do not run the desktop release pipeline.
CONVERSATION_CALENDAR_CONTEXT_READ_ENABL: default-off, and it should stay off here: it feeds Google Calendar context into conversation processing. On-prem there is no calendar integration configured, so on it would read nothing.
CONVERSATION_NOTES_V2_ENABLED: default-off, deliberate: process_conversation.py:186 via _flag_enabled(default=False) selects SummaryPipelineMode. Unset keeps LEGACY_APP_PRIMARY, which is the mode the rest of our stack was validated against. Turning it on is a product decision (it changes what a conversation summary IS), not a self-host wiring question.
CONVERSATION_OCR_CONTEXT_ENABLED: default-off: OCR meeting context, a product feature we have not wired; unset is the upstream default too.
CONVERSATION_SUMMARIZED_APP_IDS: default-ok: an allowlist of app ids for the summarized-app path; empty means none, which is the state of a self-host with no marketplace apps installed.
DD_API_KEY: default-ok: Datadog. No reader in the backend tree at all (searched); it configures the agent sidecar upstream runs. We have no such sidecar.
DESKTOP_PREVIEW_PUBLISH_KEY: default-ok: credential for publishing desktop preview builds, a pipeline we do not run.
DESKTOP_UPDATE_POINTERS_MODE: default-ok: routers/updates.py:530 defaults to 'primary'. Selects which update-pointer set the desktop client reads; we serve no desktop updates.
DESKTOP_UPDATE_RECONCILE_SAMPLE_RATE: default-ok: routers/updates.py:481 defaults to '0.01'. Sampling for a reconciler over desktop update pointers we do not publish.
FAL_KEY: default-ok: fal.ai media generation, a vendor we do not use.
GCP_LOCATION: default-ok: the region for GCP-only services (Cloud Tasks, Vertex). Nothing on the on-prem path reads a region.
GITHUB_TOKEN: default-ok: used for GitHub release lookups; the egress gate records a fallback and skips when denied (ADR-0057).
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: default-ok BY POSTURE: routers/auth.py:775 reads it with no default, and unset means the Google sign-in path is not offered. On-prem the identity provider is Keycloak/OIDC (ADR-0034); adding Google here would put a third party back on the login path.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: default-ok: the other half of GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; unset, Google sign-in is not offered.
GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY: default-ok, verified: absence is gated in utils/conversations/location.py (3203750267) so no coordinates leave the process, and callers treat None as 'unresolved'. On-prem does not have to use Google Maps.
HOSTED_PARAKEET_API_URL: NOT a silent default -- an opt-in, and the asymmetry between our two targets is deliberate. Helm declares it (values.yaml, inference.inCluster.services.*.backendEnv) but only WHEN that in-cluster service is enabled; compose cannot express 'add an env key if a profile is active', so backend.env.base documents the line to add with --profile inference. Declaring it unconditionally would be worse than leaving it unset: streaming.py:507 treats a set URL as 'parakeet is available', so a stack without the container would fail at transcription time instead of resolving cleanly. Measured on the live compose stack (no inference profile): the resolver returns (None, None, None) and records component=stt_selection to=unavailable reason=policy outcome=exhausted -- loud, and no vendor fallback (ADR-0066 holds).
HOSTED_PUSHER_API_URL: default-ok: the pusher is upstream's separate websocket fan-out service, which we do not deploy; unset, utils/pusher.py skips it. Distinct from PUSH_NOTIFICATION_BACKEND (ADR-0011/0071).
HOSTED_TRANSLATION_API_URL: same shape as HOSTED_PARAKEET_API_URL: opt-in with --profile inference (NLLB), declared conditionally by Helm, documented for compose.
HTTP_LISTEN_FINALIZATION_RUN_TIMEOUT: default-ok: main.py:255 defaults to 1500s for the finalization run. A tuning knob, not a switch; the inline dispatch path uses it as-is.
LANGCHAIN_API_KEY: default-ok: LangSmith. Governed by OMI_VENDOR_EGRESS=deny (ADR-0057), which turns the tracer off regardless of the key.
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_BYOK_ABANDONMENT_ENA: default-on is correct: services/conversation_finalization.py:305 defaults to 'true'. It gives a stranded BYOK finalization job an owner and a terminal state instead of leaving it pending forever (#12214) — a reliability behaviour that is right on any deployment, cloud or on-prem, and turning it off would only trade a recovered job for a stuck one.
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_DISPATCH_MODE: default-ok, same shape as ACCOUNT_DELETION_DISPATCH_MODE: utils/cloud_tasks.py:121, default 'inline'. Conversation finalization runs in-process.
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_ORPHAN_STALE_SECONDS: default-ok: conversation_finalization_jobs.py:107 falls back to DEFAULT_ORPHAN_RECONCILE_STALE_SECONDS, the in-code constant. Tuning for the orphan reconciler, which runs on-prem with the default.
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_TASKS_HANDLER_URL: default-ok: Cloud Tasks path only, off on-prem (LISTEN_FINALIZATION_DISPATCH_MODE=inline).
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_TASKS_INVOKER_SA: default-ok: a GCP service account for Cloud Tasks OIDC invocation; no equivalent on-prem.
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_TASKS_MAX_ATTEMPTS: default-ok: retry budget of the Cloud Tasks queue, which we do not enqueue to.
LISTEN_FINALIZATION_TASKS_QUEUE: default-ok: names a GCP Cloud Tasks queue we do not have.
MARKETPLACE_APP_REVIEWERS: default-ok: routers/users.py:1190 defaults to '' -- an empty reviewer allowlist. A self-host has no app marketplace review queue.
MCP_AUTHORIZATION_SERVER_URL: same family as MCP_RESOURCE_URL: routers/mcp_sse.py:100 defaults to 'https://api.omi.me'. Today the advertised authorization_servers comes from our OIDC issuer instead, so this default is not reached on our path -- but it is one code change away from being. Tracked with L48.
MCP_OAUTH_CHATGPT_CLIENT_ID: default-ok: seeds a built-in-OAuth client id ('omi-chatgpt-prod'); the built-in server is off under AUTH_BACKEND=oidc. See MCP_OAUTH_CLIENTS_JSON.
MCP_OAUTH_CHATGPT_REDIRECT_URIS: default-ok: redirect URIs for a built-in-OAuth client that is not served. See MCP_OAUTH_CLIENTS_JSON.
MCP_OAUTH_CLAUDE_CLIENT_ID: default-ok: seeds a built-in-OAuth client id ('omi-claude-prod'); the built-in server is off under AUTH_BACKEND=oidc.
MCP_OAUTH_CLAUDE_CLIENT_NAME: default-ok: display name of the client above.
MCP_OAUTH_CLAUDE_REDIRECT_URIS: default-ok: redirect URIs for a built-in-OAuth client that is not served.
MCP_OAUTH_CLIENTS_JSON: default-ok on our path: database/mcp_oauth.py:180 defaults to ''. It seeds the BUILT-IN MCP OAuth server, and that server is refused under AUTH_BACKEND=oidc -- measured live: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returns 'Built-in MCP OAuth server is only available with AUTH_BACKEND=firebase; use the OIDC issuer'. Clients are registered in Keycloak instead.
MCP_OAUTH_PUBLIC_CLIENT_ID: default-ok: seeds the public built-in-OAuth client id; the built-in server is off under AUTH_BACKEND=oidc.
MCP_OAUTH_PUBLIC_REDIRECT_URIS: default-ok: redirect URIs for a built-in-OAuth client that is not served.
MEETING_RECEIPT_RECONCILER_ENABLED: default-off: services/conversation_finalization.py:46 defaults to 'false'. Reconciles meeting receipts, a product feature we do not run.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_CONSOLIDATION_ENABLED: default-ok: canonical_consolidation.py:448 defaults to 'true', which is what we want -- consolidation is part of the memory pipeline L33 turned on. Declaring it would only let someone turn it off.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_GRAPH_BACKFILL_ENABLED: default-off is RIGHT for us, and the reason is scope, not preference: canonical_short_term_maintenance_cron.py:384 defaults to 'false', and what it gates is the backfill of the canonical graph for memories written BEFORE the graph existed. Historical-data migration is out of scope by decision (ADR-0001 scope note). A self-host that has been running since before the feature keeps graph-less memories until this is turned on deliberately -- which is a choice for the operator, not a default to change.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_GRAPH_BACKFILL_PAGE_SIZ: default-ok: page size of the backfill above, which is off.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_MAINTENANCE_FLEX: default-ok: canonical_short_term_maintenance_cron.py:128 defaults to 'false'. It routes the maintenance cron's LLM calls to the *_flex lanes (the long-timeout ones). Our maintenance cron runs (MEMORY_CANONICAL_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=true, L35) on the ordinary lanes, all pinned to the operator's endpoint (ADR-0067); flex only changes which lane id is used.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_PROMOTION_CRON_ENABLED: retired upstream: `--remove-env-vars` only, no reader in the backend. See MEMORY_ENABLED_USERS.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_PROMOTION_CRON_INTERVAL: retired upstream: `--remove-env-vars` only, no reader in the backend. See MEMORY_ENABLED_USERS.
MEMORY_CANONICAL_PROMOTION_FAST_TRACK_EN: retired upstream: `--remove-env-vars` only, no reader in the backend. See MEMORY_ENABLED_USERS.
MEMORY_ENABLED_USERS: retired upstream, cannot matter: it appears in backend/deploy/runtime_env.yaml ONLY inside `--remove-env-vars`, i.e. upstream deletes it from the deployed services, and no backend module reads it (searched the whole tree; the only hits are the deploy manifest and its contract test). The parity guard collects `--remove-env-vars` names on purpose -- over-collecting can only ask for a note, under-collecting would hide a variable -- so the honest answer is this note.
MEMORY_V3_CURSOR_SECRET_VERSION: default-ok: no reader in the backend (searched the tree). It is the Secret Manager VERSION pointer for MEMORY_V3_CURSOR_SECRET, which upstream's deploy resolves before injecting the value. We inject the value directly (generated like the other secrets, L34/ADR-0064), so the version pointer has nothing to point at.
MODULATE_API_KEY: default-ok, and now belt-and-braces: Modulate is the vendor STT provider. Unset it cannot be used; on top of that STT_SERVICE_MODELS=parakeet pins the local one and OMI_VENDOR_EGRESS=deny refuses the vendor outright (ADR-0066).
OMI_BACKGROUND_FLEX_CAPABLE: default-ok: promotion_flex.py:76 defaults to 'false'. It declares that the runtime can afford long background LLM calls, which upstream uses to pick flex lanes. Same reasoning as MEMORY_CANONICAL_MAINTENANCE_FLEX -- a lane-selection hint, not a capability we lose.
OMI_LLM_CHAT_AGENT_ROUTE: declared deliberately in our env, but as a NARROW pin -- see the 2026-08-09 merge note in D8. Unset it inherits the feature mode, which keeps chat on the on-prem gateway; the parity guard sees it as undeclared because we set it only in the cloud override file.
OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_ALLOW_DIRECT_MODEL_EXCEP: default-off, and that is the invariant: it would let a caller bypass the lane table and name a model directly. The whole on-prem routing posture (ADR-0067, ADR-0081) is that the backend never speaks a model name -- it sends omi:auto:<feature>. Do not declare this.
OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_CONVERSATION_ACTION_ITEM: default-off: per-feature shadow traffic; same reasoning as OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_DEV_SHADOW_ALL_ENABLED.
default-ok: sample rate of a shadow lane that is off.
OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_CONVERSATION_STRUCTURE_S: default-off: per-feature shadow traffic; same reasoning as OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_DEV_SHADOW_ALL_ENABLED.
default-ok: sample rate of a shadow lane that is off.
OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_DEV_SHADOW_ALL_ENABLED: default-off, and ON would be a defect here: shadow mode duplicates a request to a second provider to compare answers. Every lane is pinned to the operator's endpoint (ADR-0067), so the shadow would either double the load on one local model or reach a vendor. Leave unset.
OMI_LLM_GATEWAY_DEV_SHADOW_ALL_SAMPLE_RA: default-ok: sample rate of the shadow traffic above, which is off.
OMI_LLM_GPT56_EXPLICIT_CACHE_ENABLED: default-off: an OpenAI-specific prompt-cache control for a gpt-5.6 model. Our lanes serve a local model, which has no such cache.
OMI_PARITY_PACK_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS: default-ok: no reader in the backend tree (searched); an allowlist for a capture facility that is off.
OMI_PARITY_PACK_CAPTURE: default-off: the parity-pack capture is a DEV facility that records listen-session traffic for cross-platform comparison. Off is correct for a real deployment -- on, it writes transcript-derived artefacts.
OMI_PARITY_PACK_EXPORT_INTERVAL_SECONDS: default-ok: cadence of the GCS export above, which is not configured.
OMI_PARITY_PACK_GCS_URI: default-ok, and must stay unset here: it exports parity packs to a GCS bucket. On-prem there is no GCS, and the artefacts are transcript-derived.
OMI_PARITY_PACK_ROOT: default-ok: filesystem root for parity-pack captures, which are off.
PARAKEET_STREAM_ALLOCATION_PERCENT: same as PARAKEET_STREAM_CAPACITY: it configures the parakeet sidecar's admission controller, not the backend.
PARAKEET_STREAM_CAPACITY: declared by Helm for the in-cluster parakeet (values.yaml) and by the compose inference profile; the parity guard reads only the backend's own env, and this one belongs to the parakeet service.
POSTHOG_HOST: default-ok: integration_telemetry.py:186 defaults to https://app.posthog.com, and no events are sent without POSTHOG_PROJECT_API_KEY, which we do not set.
POSTHOG_PROJECT_API_KEY: default-ok: unset means product analytics never leave the box, which is the posture (ADR-0001).
PROMETHEUS_SIDECAR_PORT: default-off is correct, and it is a shape we do not have: utils/metrics.py:445 returns immediately when it is unset, so nothing is started. Set, it opens a SECOND http server bound to 127.0.0.1 for a Cloud Run sidecar to scrape. On-prem there is no sidecar and /metrics is already reachable on the backend's own surface (ADR-0068), so a loopback-only duplicate would serve nobody. Revisit with the metrics consumer work (BACKLOG L43): if the collector ever runs beside the backend rather than scraping it over the network, this is the port it would use.
PUBLIC_SHARED_CONVERSATION_CHAT_FRONTEND: default-ok: the OIDC audience of upstream's Cloud Run frontend, for a path that is off.
default-ok: a GCP service account that invokes that frontend; no equivalent on-prem.
PUBLIC_SHARED_CONVERSATION_CHAT_MODE: default-ok: selects how the public shared-conversation chat is served; unset, the gateway-invoked frontend path is not enabled. A self-host does not publish shared conversations to an anonymous frontend.
RAPID_API_HOST: default-ok: RapidAPI marketplace host for a third-party integration we do not enable.
REDIS_DB_PASSWORD: default-ok on the current network posture, and worth saying why rather than assuming: database/redis_db.py:28 passes os.getenv('REDIS_DB_PASSWORD') (None -> no AUTH) with username='default'. Our valkey is not published to the host and is reachable only on the compose `omi` network / in-cluster Service, so there is no principal to authenticate. If valkey is ever exposed, this stops being a default and becomes a gap -- it holds real state, not just cache (username ownership, webhook config, data-protection level).
SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: default-ok BY POSTURE, not by accident: it is the Google service-account credential. On-prem the document store is Mongo (ADR-0015), the object store is S3/RustFS (ADR-0032) and auth is OIDC (ADR-0034), so nothing should hold Google credentials. The four boundary guards ratchet that.
STRIPE_API_KEY: default-ok: billing. A self-host has no subscriptions to charge; unset, the Stripe paths are inert.
STRIPE_PLUS_ANNUAL_PRICE_ID: default-ok: a Stripe price id; billing is inert on-prem.
STRIPE_PLUS_MONTHLY_PRICE_ID: default-ok: a Stripe price id; billing is inert on-prem.
STRIPE_UNLIMITED_V2_ANNUAL_PRICE_ID: default-ok: a Stripe price id; billing is inert on-prem.
STRIPE_UNLIMITED_V2_MONTHLY_PRICE_ID: default-ok: a Stripe price id; billing is inert on-prem.
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: default-ok: verifies Stripe webhooks we never receive.
SYNC_BACKFILL_ENABLED: default-ON and we want it on: routers/sync.py:528/929 default to 'true'. Backfill is how a client that was offline catches up; turning it off would silently cap history at the fresh window.
SYNC_BACKFILL_GLOBAL_DAILY_HOURS: default-ok: utils/sync/backfill.py:32 defaults to '555' hours/day of aggregate backfill budget -- a fleet-scale throttle. A self-host will not approach it.
SYNC_BACKFILL_MAX_AGE_SECONDS: default-ok: utils/sync/lanes.py:41 defaults to 30 days -- how far back a backfill will reach.
SYNC_BACKFILL_USER_DAILY_HOURS: default-ok: the per-user half of the backfill budget above; the default is not reachable at self-host scale.
SYNC_CAPTURE_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECONDS: default-ok: utils/sync/lanes.py:45 defaults to 300s of tolerated client clock skew. Same value upstream runs.
SYNC_FRESH_MAX_AGE_SECONDS: default-ok: utils/sync/lanes.py:37 defaults to 6 hours -- the boundary between the fresh lane and backfill.
SYNC_LEDGER_FENCE_MODE: default-ok: the only reader is scripts/sync_ledger_fence_cutover.py, an operator tool run by hand for a staged cutover. Nothing in the serving path reads it.
SYNC_TASKS_HANDLER_URL: default-ok: Cloud Tasks path for the sync fan-out; on-prem the work runs inline.
SYNC_TASKS_INVOKER_SA: default-ok: GCP service account for Cloud Tasks OIDC invocation.
SYNC_TASKS_LOCATION: default-ok: GCP region of the Cloud Tasks queue.
SYNC_TASKS_PROJECT: default-ok: GCP project of the Cloud Tasks queue.
TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID: default-ok: Twilio voice/SMS, not part of the self-host surface.
TWILIO_TWIML_APP_SID: default-ok: Twilio TwiML app id, unused on-prem.
USE_VERTEX_AI: default-ok and load-bearing: utils/llm/providers.py:192/197 read it with default '' (falsy), so Vertex is off unless declared. Vertex is the one gateway provider that cannot be pointed at an operator endpoint (ADR-0079), so leaving this unset is what keeps that door shut.
X_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: default-ok: X/Twitter connector credential; unset, utils/x_connector.py cannot connect and the integration is simply absent.
X_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI: default-ok: the callback for the X connector, which is unconfigured.
